heading: INT. RAILWAY TELEGRAPH OFFICE, SILVER GAP, COLORADO - NIGHT (1893)

units.text: INT. RAILWAY TELEGRAPH OFFICE, SILVER GAP, COLORADO - NIGHT (1893)
A single oil lamp.
Frost feathering the window glass.
The key chatters on its brass base like a nervous bird, and a stove ticks in the corner, losing its argument with the cold.
MABEL HOLLOWAY (30s, ink on her cuffs, hair pinned tight enough to hurt) sits at the desk, one hand on the key, the other flat on a stack of unsent forms.
Across from her, REVEREND ISAIAH THORNE (60s, gaunt, black coat gone green at the seams) stands with his hat held against his chest as though it might be asked for.
It has been four hours.
units.name: THORNE

units.text: I know how long it's been, Reverend.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Then you know the whole town is gathered at the church, waiting to be told something.
units.name: THORNE

units.text: Then they'll wait.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: The key stops.
She lifts her hand from it as if it had grown hot.
Miss Holloway. A telegram arrives from the mine company. You read it. And now you will not tell me what it says.
units.name: THORNE

units.text: It isn't addressed to you.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: It is addressed to forty families.
units.name: THORNE

units.text: Mabel looks at the paper under her palm.
She does not move her hand.
It's addressed to the superintendent. He isn't here to receive it.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Then I will carry it to him.
units.name: THORNE

units.text: He's in the shaft.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Silence.
The stove ticks.
Thorne lowers his hat, slowly, onto the desk.
Ah.
units.name: THORNE

units.text: The door bangs open.
SHERIFF GUS ARMBRUSTER (50s, mustache full of snow, a badge he never polishes) stamps in, breathing hard, and shoves the door shut with his shoulder.
Lights are out on the whole ridge. Somebody's cut the line past the trestle.
units.name: ARMBRUSTER

units.text: It wasn't cut. It was buried.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Buried?
units.name: ARMBRUSTER

units.text: Slide came down at nine. I felt the wire go slack under my hand.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: And you didn't think to say?
units.name: ARMBRUSTER

units.text: I said to Reverend Thorne. Four hours ago. He didn't ask what I meant.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Thorne looks at the floor.
Armbruster takes off his gloves one finger at a time, then looks at the stove, and then at the key.
Can you raise anyone?
units.name: ARMBRUSTER

units.text: I've been trying since nine.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: She taps out a short burst.
Nothing.
She taps again.
The key answers with a faint, dry, stuttering click, as though someone far away had leaned on the other end by accident.
The three of them go still.
...Silver Gap... Silver Gap, this is Division at Leadville... come back...
units.name: DISPATCHER

units.text: Mabel seizes the key.
Armbruster is at her shoulder in two strides.
Thorne's lips begin to move, soundless.
Division, this is Holloway at Gap. Line is restored. Repeat, line is restored.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: ...Holloway, we had you for dead. Report conditions...
units.name: DISPATCHER

units.text: Tell him about the slide. Tell him about the mine.
units.name: ARMBRUSTER

units.text: I'm telling him.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: ...say again, conditions at Number Four shaft...
units.name: DISPATCHER

units.text: Mabel's hand hesitates above the key.
She glances at Thorne, then at the paper on the desk, then back at the key.
Read it to him, Miss Holloway.
units.name: THORNE

units.text: Reverend--
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Read it. Whatever it says. Better he hears it from us than from a stranger.
units.name: THORNE

units.text: Mabel slides the paper out from under her palm, finally.
Unfolds it.
Her eyes travel across it once.
She folds it again.
Fourteen men underground at the time of the slide.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Fourteen.
units.name: ARMBRUSTER

units.text: Superintendent among them. Rescue party left Leadville at six. They are expected at dawn.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: The door opens a third time.
A gust, a flurry of snow, and ROSALIND PEMBERTON (20s, bare-headed, carrying a lantern and a baby wrapped in a shawl) stands on the threshold.
Her hair is wet with melt, and her face is entirely composed, which is worse than if it were not.
Mr. Armbruster. They said you'd be here.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Mrs. Pemberton. You shouldn't be out in this.
units.name: ARMBRUSTER

units.text: My husband is Number Four's night boss. I want to know if anyone has heard from Number Four.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Nobody answers.
Thorne takes a step toward her.
Armbruster sets his gloves on the desk.
Mabel keeps her eyes on the key.
I've been in this town six years. I know what it sounds like when no one is answering.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Mrs. Pemberton, the line has only just come back. We know almost nothing.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Then tell me almost.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Mabel stands, and for the first time her voice cracks and she does not hide it.
Fourteen men were below. The rescue party leaves Leadville at dawn. That's all that is known.
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Fourteen.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: She looks down at the baby, who is asleep.
She adjusts the shawl with great care.
Then I will wait with the others. Reverend, will you take me to the church?
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: It would be an honor.
units.name: THORNE

units.text: ...Gap, do you copy... Gap...
units.name: DISPATCHER

units.text: Mabel sits.
Her fingers find the key.
Rosalind and Thorne go out into the snow, and Armbruster holds the door for them, watching their lantern shrink up the hill.
Dawn.
units.name: ARMBRUSTER

units.text: He shuts the door.
The stove ticks.
The key begins, once more, to chatter.
